manuscript.introduction:
This review asks: In adults with hypertriglyceridemia, does AMR101 (ethyl icosapentate) - 4 g/day compared with placebo affect difference between amr101 (ethyl icosapentate) and placebo treatment groups in triglyceride lowering effect?

It pools 2 randomised trials, against not recorded on the page this object was extracted from.

The outcome pooled is Difference Between AMR101 (Ethyl Icosapentate) and Placebo Treatment Groups in Triglyceride Lowering Effect.

Everything in this paragraph is derived from stored fields and none of it is authored. The interpretive sentences that follow are marked as drafts and are the author's to replace.

risk_of_bias.tool: RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials)

NCT01047683.result_assessed: percentage change in fasting serum triglycerides at Week 12 -- a SCHEDULED LABORATORY MEASUREMENT, not an adjudicated clinical event
NCT01047683.registered_masking: QUADRUPLE -- participant, care provider, investigator, OUTCOMES ASSESSOR

D1_randomisation_process.reason: allocation: RANDOMIZED is recorded on the registry design module for both trials, not merely implied by a title. Arm sizes are consistent with a concealed sequence.
D1_randomisation_process.what_is_NOT_established: The concealment MECHANISM is not described on the registry. LOW is scored on the recorded allocation and the balance, not on a mechanism nobody here has read.

resolved_2026_08_21.the_text_that_decides_it: RoB 2 guidance 2019, Box 4, signalling question 1.1: "Answer 'No information' if the only information about randomization methods is a statement that the study is randomized." And section 4.4: "A judgement of low risk of bias requires that the trial has an adequate method of concealing the allocation sequence from those involved in enrolling participants, and there are no concerns about generation of the allocation sequence." Cochrane Handbook 6.5 section 8.3 names the domain's three components.
resolved_2026_08_21.why_this_is_not_an_adjudicated_dispute: A blind second assessor from a different model family disagreed with this domain on 89% of judgements across 22 topics. THAT WOULD ORDINARILY BE A DISPUTE TO ADJUDICATE. It is not one: the tool's own text names this exact evidential situation -- a bare statement that a study was randomised -- and prescribes the answer. The second assessor is not being deferred to; the guidance is being applied.
resolved_2026_08_21.what_the_registry_gives_and_does_not: A ClinicalTrials.gov design module records `allocation: RANDOMIZED`. It carries no sequence-generation method and no allocation-concealment mechanism. The original judgement's own note said so before scoring LOW.
resolved_2026_08_21.how_this_maps_to_the_tool_s_algorithm: The tool maps 'No information' on 1.1 and 1.2 with no baseline concern to a DOMAIN judgement of SOME CONCERNS. This project writes NO_INFORMATION on the domain when it could not be judged from the sources read, and caps the OVERALL at SOME_CONCERNS. Same place, and it keeps 'we could not judge this' distinguishable from 'we judged it and had concerns'.
resolved_2026_08_21.what_does_not_change: NO OVERALL RATING AND NO GRADE CERTAINTY MOVES. All 51 judgements were already capped at SOME_CONCERNS or HIGH by another NO_INFORMATION domain.
resolved_2026_08_21.what_would_close_it_properly: The trial publications or protocols, which carry sequence generation and concealment. Neither was read. Until one is, LOW is not available on this domain for any result in this corpus.
resolved_2026_08_21.and_this_one_also_inferred_concealment_f: This judgement cited, in addition, that the arm sizes are balanced and that this is what a concealed sequence produces. THAT IS AN INFERENCE, NOT A REGISTRY FACT. Balanced arms are CONSISTENT WITH concealment and do not establish it, and RoB 2 signalling question 1.3 asks whether baseline DIFFERENCES suggest a problem -- a different question from whether concealment was adequate. The entry states in its own words that the mechanism was never read.

D2_deviations_from_intended_intervention.basis: NOT ESTABLISHED -- THE REGISTRY DOES NOT DESCRIBE IT
D2_deviations_from_intended_intervention.reason: Neither registration states the analysis population or how deviations were handled. THIS OBSTACLE IS IN THE EVIDENCE AVAILABLE ON THE REGISTRY, and it is NOT the same as the empagliflozin case, where the methods section exists and is behind a paywall. Here the registry simply does not carry the field. The exit is the published papers -- Bays 2011 (PMID 21683321) for MARINE and the ANCHOR report for the second -- and neither has been read.

D3_missing_outcome_data.basis: NOT ESTABLISHED -- AND THE ENDPOINT SHAPE IS WHY IT MATTERS HERE
D3_missing_outcome_data.reason: The result is a FIXED-TIMEPOINT MEASUREMENT at Week 12, not a time-to-event with censoring. A participant who leaves before Week 12 has NO VALUE -- they do not contribute partial follow-up the way an EMPEROR participant does. So missing outcome data is a live threat for this result in a way it is not for an adjudicated event, and neither registration states how many Week-12 values were missing or how they were handled. THE SAME DOMAIN, A DIFFERENT RISK, BECAUSE THE ENDPOINT IS A DIFFERENT KIND OF THING.

D4_measurement_of_the_outcome.reason: The outcome is fasting serum triglyceride measured by laboratory assay. The registry records the OUTCOMES ASSESSOR as masked, and an automated assay on a fasting sample is not a measurement an assessor's expectation can shade in any case. THIS IS NOT EMPEROR'S REASON -- there the judgement rested on adjudication of clinical events by a blinded committee. Same domain, different evidence, different argument.

D5_selection_of_the_reported_result.basis: REGISTRATION COMPARED WITH WHAT THIS OBJECT POOLS
D5_selection_of_the_reported_result.reason: The registered primary is a MEDIAN PERCENT CHANGE and this object pools a MEAN DIFFERENCE. And both trials registered THREE ARMS -- placebo, 2 g/day, 4 g/day -- while this object records two, so a dose arm was selected with no record of the selection. A result reported on a different summary statistic from the registered one, drawn from a multi-arm trial with an unrecorded arm choice, is the domain RoB 2's D5 exists to flag. NOT HIGH: the direction was not chosen after seeing the data as far as anything read shows, and inventing that would be the accusing-direction error.

adjudicated_2026_08_21.why: The registered primary-outcome count is not on this entry, so the discriminator cannot be applied. REPORTED AS UNRESOLVED rather than settled by preference; both judgements stand and both render.
adjudicated_2026_08_21.discriminator: WHICH ASSESSOR'S REASON CITES A REGISTRY FACT. Both were asked; assessor 2's stated bases were collected in a second blind round rather than assumed. The count of registered primary outcomes is a field on the registration and is not a matter of judgement.

grade.approach: GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons.

steps.reason: BOTH results are SOME_CONCERNS and the driver is NOT empagliflozin's. D5 is SOME_CONCERNS in its own right: the registered primary is a MEDIAN percent change and this pool is a MEAN difference, and both trials registered THREE arms where the object records two. D2 and D3 are additionally NO_INFORMATION -- and D3 here is a live threat rather than a formality, because a week-12 laboratory value is missing when a participant leaves, where a time-to-event result absorbs the same withdrawal by censoring.

I-squared is 64.2% with tau-squared 43.19 over k=2. Handbook 10.10.2 warns against reading I-squared mechanically, and at this k the estimate is imprecise -- but the point estimates themselves differ materially and the direction of the finding does not rest on the statistic alone.

THE POOLED QUANTITY IS NOT THE REGISTERED QUANTITY. Both registrations describe the primary as a MEDIAN PERCENT CHANGE from baseline to week 12 in fasting serum triglycerides; this pool is a MEAN DIFFERENCE. In populations selected on a triglyceride threshold -- above 500 mg/dL in MARINE, above 200 in ANCHOR -- the mean and the median diverge BY CONSTRUCTION, which is precisely why a trialist reports a median. THE POOL THEREFORE ANSWERS A QUESTION NEITHER TRIAL ASKED, and that is an indirectness fact, not a footnote. Compounded by a dose arm selected from three registered arms with the selection recorded nowhere.

k=2, and the interval -36.84 to -14.84 spans a 22-point range on a percentage change. Two trials of 229 and 702 participants do not meet an optimal information size for an effect reported as a percentage of a skewed baseline. Handbook 15.6.2.

NOT ASSESSED RATHER THAN ASSESSED AS ABSENT. Funnel-plot asymmetry and its tests are uninformative below about ten studies -- Handbook 13.3.5.4 -- and these pools carry two or three. 'Undetected' here means NOBODY LOOKED WITH AN INSTRUMENT THAT COULD SEE, not that publication bias is unlikely. Not rated down, because rating down on an unmeasurable domain would invent a defect.

primary.summary: Certainty VERY_LOW. The risk-of-bias domain reads the per-result RoB 2 assessments made 2026-08-20 and named above, not a topic-level summary; indirectness reads the estimand findings recorded on this pool.

grade.not_rated_up: No domain is rated UP. Rating up for a large effect or a dose-response gradient applies to observational evidence that has not already been rated down, and neither condition holds here.
grade.WHY_THESE_THREE_RATINGS_DIFFER: empagliflozin is the only one of the three with NO recorded estimand problem and the only one with I-squared of zero, so its indirectness and inconsistency are not serious where the other two are. inclisiran is the only one meeting an optimal information size, so its imprecision is not serious where the other two are. IF THE THREE RATINGS WERE IDENTICAL THE RATING WOULD NOT BE READING THE ASSESSMENTS.
